chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Fadhal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Abdul Mu'min al-Ansari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Batḥā' of Mecca was presented to me as gold, so I said: 'O Lord, no, but rather I shall be satiated one day and hungry one day. When I am satiated, I will praise You and give thanks to You, and when I am hungry, I will supplicate to You and remember You.'

key_terms.أَجُوعُ: I will be hungry, representing need and deprivation.
key_terms.أَشْبَعُ: I will be satiated/full, representing comfort and ease.
key_terms.بَطْحَاءُ: A plain or valley in Mecca, often associated with the site of the Kaaba or the surrounding area.
key_terms.حَمِدْتُكَ: I praised You, expressing gratitude for blessings.
key_terms.دَعَوْتُكَ: I supplicated to You, asking for needs during times of hunger.
key_terms.ذَكَرْتُكَ: I remembered You, engaging in dhikr during times of need.
key_terms.ذَهَباً: Gold, representing worldly wealth and material abundance.
key_terms.شَكَرْتُكَ: I gave thanks to You, acknowledging divine favors.

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet decline the offer of gold for Batḥā?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s (saww) strategic choice of a balanced asceticism, where alternating states of satiety and hunger serve as distinct spiritual disciplines. In Shia tradition, this reflects the principle that comfort fosters gratitude (shukr) while needfulness cultivates humble supplication (du'a), ensuring constant divine connection regardless of material circumstances. It underscores the Prophetic model of using worldly conditions as tools for spiritual elevation rather than ends in themselves.

en.hubeali: H 14550 – Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn fazzaal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from Abdul Mo’min Al-Ansary, who has said: Abu Abdullahasws having said:

‘The Rasoolsaww Allahazwj said: ‘There were presented to mesaww Bat’ha and Makka of gold. So Isaww said: ‘O Lordazwj! No, but Isaww would like to satiate one day and remain hungry one day, for if Isaww am satiated Isaww would thank Youazwj, and if Isaww am hungry, Isaww would supplicate to Youazwj and Remember Youazwj’. out of 567
en.sarwar: 102. Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn fazzaal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from Abdul Mo’min Al-Ansary, who has said:

Abu Abdullah (a.s.) having said: ‘The Rasool (saww) Allah (azwj) said: ‘There were presented to me (saww) Bat’ha and Makka of gold. So I (saww) said: ‘O Lord (azwj)! No, but I (saww) would like to satiate one day and remain hungry one day, for if I (saww) am satiated I (saww) would thank You (azwj), and if I (saww) am hungry, I (saww) would supplicate to You (azwj) and Remember You (azwj)’.
